h: פָּרָשַׁת פָּרָה, מַאֲמָר ד׳ Parshas Parah — Maamar Daled

p: In Pesikta Rabbasi on Parshas Parah
and the statute He gave them' (Tehillim 99:6–7).
that the Torah was written in his name, etc.;
and for Shmuel a book was written:
'And he wrote it in the book
and placed it before Hashem' (I Shmuel 10:25)."
That is, the law of the kingship
"But regarding Aharon we have not heard;
that this parsha was given to him,
that it shall not depart from him,
until the end of all the generations:
'This is the statute of the Torah.'"
the parsha of the Parah applies
רַק בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ הָיָה קַיָּים
only when the Beis HaMikdash was standing,
and the ashes of the Parah have been hidden from us.
אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה
HaKadosh Baruch Hu said to Moshe:
for greater than this you are prepared, etc.
but the lamps are forever, etc.
And all the blessings I gave you
but the lamps of the Beis HaMikdash,
they have already raised the difficulty on this,
for they ceased with the Churban.
that it refers to the Chanukah lights —
the difficulty on this was already raised
in the Alshich (Bamidbar ibid.); see there.
And we have said that the matter of the lamps of the Mikdash
alludes to the light of Torah she'b'al peh,
for HaKadosh Baruch Hu, as it were,
that he should light up in the heart of Yisrael
the light of Torah she'b'al peh;
"For the lips of the kohen," etc.,
"and they shall seek Torah from his mouth"
(and it was explained in Chanukah, maamar 1,
And so too the matter of Birkas Kohanim.
For it is "May Hashem bless you" (Bamidbar 6:24) —
like the blessing of the fish
and so here, "May He bless you"
in the manner of what is said:
"For the lips of the kohen shall guard knowledge."
That is, he will guard the purity
which is called by the name "daas,"
in the manner of what they said (Shabbos 31a):
For Chochmah is called the Supernal Holiness
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קכא, א)
for the utterance "Let there be light"
corresponds to the attribute of Chochmah,
which is the beginning of recognition,
for it is the intellect hidden
in the utterance "Let there be light"
correspond to the five Chumashei Torah
in which the "abundance of wisdom" comes
to purify and repair the "abundance of anger."
For in truth everything is included
and the essence of what they said (Kiddushin 30b),
and I created Torah as its antidote,"
And were it not for the corruption,
the five Chumashei Torah would have sufficed
so that they not be delivered into its hand.
and it became necessary to repair the "abundance of anger"
did they need the "abundance of wisdom"
וְזֶה דַּעַת שֶׁפֵּירֵשׁ רַשִׁ״י (כִּי תִשָּׂא לא, ג)
And this is "daas," which Rashi explained (Ki Sisa 31:3)
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג סא, א)
(בָּבָא בַּתְרָא יב, א דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל הָא)
that is, it receives from Torah she'b'chsav,
And about this it is said:
"For the lips of the kohen shall guard knowledge" —
that he guards the purity of Yisrael,
emptying out the evil from the fool's heart.
and this is what they said, "and guard you" —
that it not enter the heart, "the fool's at his left."
And this is through the aspect of Daas,
which one merits by joining the wisdom in the mind
with the understanding in the heart.
And from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
through which Torah study was implanted in their heart,
through which the yetzer hara was uprooted from their heart
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה, א, טו)
And so Hashem Yisbarach formed the souls:
But from the side of man,
and love from the side of Hashem Yisbarach —
(יְרוּשַׁלְמִי שְׁקָלִים פֶּרֶק ג הֲלָכָה ג יד, ב)
'and he shall purify it and sanctify it.'"
And so the order of the Shabbos meals:
[פְּרִי עֵץ חַיִּים שַׁעַר הַשַּׁבָּת פֶּרֶק יז]
that of Shabbos night, for Yitzchak,
for the whole essence of Torah she'b'al peh
שֶׁאַף עַל כְּתוּבִים אִיתָא (תַּעֲנִית ט, א)
so that even about the Kesuvim it says (Taanis 9a):
that is not alluded to in the Torah?"
that for this reason it is said
in the parsha of the lamps (Shemos 27:20),
"And they shall take to you oil," etc.
(as was explained in Parshas Tetzaveh, maamar 1),
to Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
and he gives the power to Aharon,
who is the groomsman of the Queen,
the light of Torah she'b'al peh —
And this is the matter of reading
And it says in the Yerushalmi
(מְגִילָּה פֶּרֶק ג הֲלָכָה ה כה, ב)
for on the first of Nisan the Mishkan was erected,
and on the second the Parah was burned.
So why does Parah come first?
Because it is the purification of all Yisrael."
what kind of answer is this
when we have no Mikdash and no ashes of the Parah?
And if we merit that the Mikdash be built,
they will make known the place of the Parah's ashes,
and their purification will precede Pesach.
that since it is written "This is the statute of the Torah,"
and not "This is the statute of the Parah,"
כְּעֵין דִּכְתִיב זֹאת חֻקַּת הַפֶּסַח [שְׁמוֹת יב, מג]
as it is written "This is the statute of the Pesach" (Shemos 12:43),
in the manner of what we find
שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַחַטָּאת [וַיִּקְרָא ו, יח]
that they expounded: "This is the law of the sin-offering" (Vayikra 6:18)
and "This is the law of the guilt-offering" (ibid. 7:1) —
"Whoever occupies himself with the law of the sin-offering
is as though he offered a sin-offering,
And likewise, "This is the law of the burnt-offering" (ibid. 37):
So too it is alluded to here,
in what they said, "This is the statute of the Torah,"
that through the reading of the parsha
it will be as though the kohen
And similar to what we find
and you raise up their heads,
that they read it before Me,
it is as though you stand there
and raise up their heads," etc.
That is, the reading of the parsha accomplishes,
together with the longing in the heart
to fulfill it when one is able,
as though he fulfilled it in deed
from the tumah of the soul.
And this is what they said:
"For it is the purification of all Yisrael."
And from here there is support and basis
that the reading of Parshas Parah is d'Oraisa,
And this is what they said in the Yerushalmi,
for it is the purification of Yisrael;
which is the beginning of the words of Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב לט, ב)
that it needed to begin only
from "This month shall be for you."
And from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
which is the words of Torah,
that from the side of Hashem Yisbarach
But from the side of Yisrael
for it is the purification of Yisrael,
And this is what they said in the Pesikta,
that there was given to Aharon
that it shall not depart from him
until the end of all the generations.
For the matter of this parsha
even at a time when there is no Mikdash,
the reading of the Torah-portion of the Parah is effective,
as though the Parah were made
And in this parsha it also says,
"And they shall take to you a cow," etc.,
to Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
who is the groomsman of the King,
who brought down the Torah she'b'chsav
who is the groomsman of the Queen
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג נג, ב)
"For the lips of the kohen shall guard knowledge,
and they shall seek Torah from his mouth."
regarding the parsha of the lamps,
"And they shall take to you oil," etc.,
וְעַל יְדֵי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and through Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
the power was transmitted to Aharon,
And Parshas Parah is read on Shabbos,
of Kudsha Brich Hu and His Shechinah;
וְעַל כֵּן אוֹמְרִים [בַּזֶּמֶר הָאֲרִ״י לְלֵיל שַׁבָּת]
and therefore we say (in the Arizal's zemer for Shabbos night),
who are Moshe, groomsman of the King,
and Aharon, groomsman of the Queen,
and corresponding to the two groomsmen," etc.
that the Torah was given on Shabbos,
we call it Torah she'b'al peh."
And when there are groom and bride,
and then is the time of "the statute of the Torah,"
that the words of Torah be engraved in the heart.
And this is what is said:

paragraphs.text: Bava Batra 14b — “Who wrote them? Moshe wrote his book, the section of Bilam, and Iyov. Yehoshua wrote his book and eight verses of the Torah. Shmuel wrote his book, Shoftim, and Rus.”

paragraphs.text: Pesikta Rabbasi 14:11, Parah — “We have heard of Moshe that Torah was written in his name: Remember the Torah of My servant Moshe. Of Shmuel a book was written: He wrote it in a book and placed it before Hashem. But we have heard nothing of this concerning Aharon. Rather, it teaches that this section was given to him, never to depart from him, his children, or his children's children until the end of all generations.” The Midrash expounds They kept His testimonies and a statute He gave them. Rav Tzadok asks how the heifer's teaching remains active after the Temple's destruction.

paragraphs.text: Bamidbar Rabbah 15:6 — “The Holy One, blessed be He, told Moshe: Go, tell Aharon, Do not fear; you are destined for a greatness beyond this. ... The offerings are practiced while the Temple stands, but the lamps are forever: The seven lamps shall give light toward the face of the Menorah. All the blessings I gave you to bless My children will never cease.” The Midrash speaks of both the lamps and the priestly blessing as enduring. Rav Tzadok examines how that language applies when the Temple lamps are no longer lit.

paragraphs.text: Ramban, Bamidbar 8:2 — “It is well known that when the Temple does not stand and the offerings cease because of its destruction, the lamps also cease. Rather, the Sages alluded only to the lamps of the Chanukah of the Chashmonaim, which are observed even after the destruction, during our exile. Likewise the priestly blessing, adjacent to the princes' dedication, is observed forever.”

paragraphs.text: Alshich, Bamidbar 8, Behaaloscha — “It is difficult: the Midrash says the lamps endure forever, but the Menorah too ceased at the destruction. If this means the Chanukah lamps, there are eight of them: how can it identify them with The seven lamps shall give light? Moreover, they are not performed by priests alone, and they are only a memorial and of rabbinic origin: how are they mentioned in Torah? ... When the sanctuary below was established, a sanctuary above was established. When the lamps were kindled below, those above were kindled and remained burning forever from that kindling.” Alshich raises explicit objections to the Chanukah reading and explains the lasting supernal effect of Aharon's kindling. Rav Tzadok offers the enduring light of Oral Torah as his interpretation.

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 31a — “Reish Lakish said: What is meant by Faithfulness of your times, strength, salvations, wisdom, and knowledge? Faithfulness is Zeraim; your times is Moed; strength is Nashim; salvations is Nezikin; wisdom is Kodashim; knowledge is Taharos. Even so, The fear of Hashem is His treasure.”

paragraphs.text: Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2:4, Rabbi Nechemyah — “Rabbi Nechemyah said: When Israel heard You shall have no other, the evil inclination was uprooted from their hearts. They came to Moshe and said: Moshe our teacher, become an intermediary, a messenger between us, as it is said, You speak with us, and we shall hear; and, Now why should we die? What benefit is there in our being lost? Immediately the evil inclination returned to its place. They came back to Moshe and said: If only He would reveal Himself to us a second time! If only He would kiss me with the kisses of His mouth! He told them: This is not for now, but for the future to come, as it is written, I shall remove the heart of stone from your flesh.” This is the distinct Rabbi Nechemyah teaching concerning Lo yihyeh. The preceding Rabbi Yehudah teaching concerns Torah becoming fixed in the heart at Anochi. The manuscript's 1:15 numbering differs from this digital division,1:2:4.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Mei HaShiloach, vol. I, Bo — “By reason, a person cannot grasp ‘I am Hashem’ before his heart is cleansed of ‘You shall have no other gods’… but Hashem in His great mercy put ‘I am’ first.” The Izhbitzer draws the same two orders as Rav Tzadok. From man’s side purity comes first. From Hashem’s side the light is given first, so that the heart can then be cleansed.

paragraphs.text: Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 3:3 — “Purity leads to holiness, as it is written, He shall purify it and sanctify it. Holiness leads to humility, as it is written, High and holy is His Name ... and with the contrite and humble of spirit.” The chain describes a path of human preparation. Rav Tzadok distinguishes it from Divine bestowal, where holiness precedes purification.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Terumah 6 — “The Arizal assigned the Friday-night meal to Yitzchak and the Shabbos-morning meal to Avraham, though the order of the Avos is Avraham, Yitzchak… for that is the order from Yisrael’s side, to repair the corruption.” Rav Tzadok gives the same reason there for the Arizal’s order. Fear and purification, Yitzchak’s trait, come first from below. Avraham’s kindness and wisdom follow.

paragraphs.text: Taanit 9a — “Rabbi Yochanan sat wondering. He said: Is there anything written in the Writings that is not alluded to in Torah? The child answered: Is this not alluded to? It is written, Their hearts went out, and they trembled to one another, saying, What is this that God has done to us?” The exchange concerns a verse in Mishlei. Rav Tzadok draws from it the principle that later revelation is rooted in Torah.

paragraphs.text: Menachot 110a — “Reish Lakish said: What is meant by ‘This is the Torah for the burnt offering, for the meal offering, for the sin offering, and for the guilt offering’? Whoever occupies himself with Torah is as though he offered a burnt offering, a meal offering, a sin offering, and a guilt offering. Rava said: ... Whoever occupies himself with Torah requires neither a burnt offering, nor a meal offering, nor a guilt offering. Rabbi Yitzchak said: What is meant by ‘This is the Torah of the sin offering’ and ‘This is the Torah of the guilt offering’? Whoever occupies himself with the Torah of a sin offering is as though he offered a sin offering; whoever occupies himself with the Torah of a guilt offering is as though he offered a guilt offering.” This supplies Rav Tzadok's analogy for reading the heifer's section when the physical rite cannot be performed.

paragraphs.text: Shulchan Aruch and Rema, Orach Chaim 685:7 — “Some say that Parshas Zachor and Parshas Parah Adumah must be read by Torah law. Therefore residents of settlements without a minyan must come to a place with a minyan on these Shabbosos to hear these sections, which are of Torah obligation. Rema: If they cannot come, they should nevertheless take care to read them with their melody and cantillation.” Shulchan Aruch records this as some say. Rav Tzadok offers support for that opinion; he does not erase the disagreement implied by that formulation.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Rabbi Shmuel Bornsztain, Shem MiShmuel, Ki Tisa–Parah 5671 — “Pesach means a leap, as Rashi explains: they attained divine understanding beyond their own level. Consequently this did not come through self-effacement and submission, for self-effacement and submission correspond to one's own level. While they were still in Egypt, they could not reach the self-effacement required for the great understanding they then attained; only at the giving of the Torah did they reach that self-effacement. Perhaps this is why the first festival day of Pesach is called Shabbos in Scripture, for in this respect the two are alike. This explains the Yerushalmi's statement that HaChodesh should properly precede Parah: Pesach does not come through the aspect of Parah. Yet Parah is Israel's purification, since the foundation and root of Israel's service is that they make themselves small. Although the Egyptian Pesach came without the aspect of Parah, when they merit to make themselves small and efface themselves, their understanding on Pesach becomes greater still.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Rav Tzadok distinguishes the Divine order, in which the gift of Torah precedes purification, from Israel's order, in which Parah must come first. Shem MiShmuel develops the same reversed order through Pesach as a Divine leap beyond Israel's attained level. His explanation makes the role of prior purification precise: freely bestowed illumination can arrive before that preparation, while Israel's own humble preparation enlarges its reception of the gift.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 53b, Metzora 7, s.v. Ta chazi — “Consider the difference between Moshe and Aharon, and which is higher. Moshe is higher: Moshe is the King's attendant, and Aharon the Queen's attendant. This is compared to a king who had an exalted queen. He gave her an attendant to prepare her and attend to the affairs of the household. Therefore, when this attendant enters before the king, he enters only with the queen: With this Aharon shall enter.” Rav Tzadok relates the attendants' complementary tasks to Written Torah brought down through Moshe and Israel's purification through Aharon.

paragraphs.text: Azamer BiShvachin, Shabbos-night zemer — “Great joy will come, a double portion; light will reach her, and abundant blessings. Come near, bridal attendants; make the preparations, to increase the kinds, fish and other living creatures. To make souls and new spirits, through thirty-two and through three branches.” The song directly invites the shushvinin, the bridal attendants. Rav Tzadok identifies them here with Moshe and Aharon in the divine union of Shabbos.
